title: 4 × 6 Photo at 300 DPI: Start with 1200 × 1800 Pixels
description: A borderless 4 × 6 inch photo at 300 pixels per inch needs 1200 × 1800 pixels.
direct: A borderless 4 × 6 inch photo at 300 pixels per inch needs 1200 × 1800 pixels. Multiply each dimension in inches by 300. Changing the DPI tag alone does not create those pixels or add detail to a small image.
figureAlt: A 4 by 6 inch photo at 300 pixels per inch requires 1200 by 1800 pixels.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export.
cards.choice.heading: Check shape as well as pixels
cards.choice.body: A 4 × 6 print has a 2:3 aspect ratio. A differently shaped original needs cropping or borders. Inspect faces near the edges before accepting a crop.
sections.explain.heading: Work the numbers
sections.explain.body: 4 × 300 = 1200 and 6 × 300 = 1800. The same 1200 × 1800 pixels at 200 pixels per inch describe a 6 × 9 inch image. The pixel data has not gained detail merely because the physical-size metadata changed. The app uses DPI terminology; image sampling is more precisely pixels per inch.
sections.practice.heading: Proof before a large order
sections.practice.body: Our iPhone app supports print-size fitting, crop confirmation and export verification, plus a 4 × 6 PDF proof with a 100 mm ruler. Print the proof at 100%; printer settings can still change the result. Basic single-photo DPI edits are free. Print-size fitting is an advanced export, with three successful advanced exports free before Pro. Space Sheep Studio develops the app. Resampling enlarges the pixel grid but cannot recreate missing captured detail.

steps.step-1.text: In DPI: Photo Print Prep, choose a 4 × 6 inch target and 300 DPI; decide whether you need white borders.
steps.step-2.text: Review the crop and pixel sufficiency. Keep pixels, lower the target DPI or resample according to the print requirement.
steps.step-3.text: Export and read back the actual dimensions and both DPI axes. Inspect the file and confirm the print service’s scaling settings.
